definition: How quickly a person can take in information, process it, and respond.
common_impairment_signs: takes longer to complete simple tasks
difficulty keeping up with fast conversations or instructions
biological_basis: Slowed processing speed in VCI is often driven by cerebrovascular damage to frontal–subcortical circuits and disrupted white-matter tracts.
source_note: ReCOGnAIze development data show processing speed and response-time variability as key VCI markers.

definition: The set of skills that help with planning, organizing, switching between tasks, and staying on track.
measured_by_tasks: complex multi-step game elements (e.g., Grocery Shopping planning)
biological_basis: Executive skills rely on frontal–subcortical loops that are vulnerable to vascular injury, causing problems even when memory is relatively preserved.
source_note: BIOCIS analysis found greater executive deficits in VCI compared to non-vascular cognitive impairment.

definition: Ability to stay focused, ignore distractions, and stop oneself from reacting too quickly.
common_impairment_signs: pressing/swiping even when they know they should wait
more mistakes when tasks get faster
biological_basis: Impulse dyscontrol in high vascular burden is linked to disrupted inhibitory pathways and white-matter lesions.
source_note: Airplane go/no-go in ReCOGnAIze targets inhibitory control, a common issue in patients with high WMH burden.

definition: Ability to learn, store, and recall information over short and longer delays.
biological_basis: Memory can be secondarily affected in VCI, especially when vascular injury co-exists with neurodegenerative processes.
source_note: ReCOGnAIze composite score detects MCI more accurately than MoCA.

definition: Vascular health refers to the body's ability to maintain healthy blood vessels and good blood flow, which is critical for brain function.

risk_factors.label: High blood pressure
risk_factors.brief_effect: Can make blood vessels narrow and stiff, reducing blood flow to the brain.

risk_factors.label: High cholesterol
risk_factors.brief_effect: Can cause plaque build-up that clogs arteries, limiting blood flow.

risk_factors.label: Obesity
risk_factors.brief_effect: Increases blood pressure and cholesterol, and promotes inflammation.

risk_factors.label: Diabetes
risk_factors.brief_effect: Damages blood vessels and raises blood sugar, harming vessel walls.

risk_factors.label: Smoking
risk_factors.brief_effect: Harms the lining of blood vessels, raises blood pressure, and reduces oxygen delivery.

brain_impact_summary: All of these factors can reduce blood flow to the brain and may increase the risk of memory and cognitive problems, including stroke and vascular cognitive impairment.
disclaimer: This information is educational and does not diagnose any disease. Results should be interpreted only by a qualified healthcare professional.
